newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges lower, crosses dominate.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges lower, crosses dominate.

text.p: White sugar futures were reluctant to stray too far from their opening ranges on Tuesday afternoon and the session was mostly confined to commission house crosses and routine spread dealings, traders said.
The crosses, some of which were on the forward spreads, accounted for the bulk of the solid volume, which by 1605 GMT totalled 2,272 lots.
Business was otherwise routine with London traders watching the fortunes of the New York market after the October expiry.
Unless the March raws contract -- now the spot position -- rallied up to 10.95 cents/lb, little bullish sentiment could be expected in London, they said.
"There's been some bits and pieces, some switch trading here and there," said one trader.
December was 90 cents weaker at $323.70 and March was down $1.30 at $320.50.
In physical news, Jordan and Syria are both slated to hold buying tenders on Wednesday.
Sri Lanka is also in the market on that day to buy 12,500 tonnes of refined whites for first half December shipment.
All traded positions lost ground in Paris where market volume reached 660 lots.
December was down $1.70 at $324.00 and March down $2.70 $320.50.
